title: Fortigon update: turning an AI-assisted Godot project into a playable tower-defense / FPS demo
author: RAGA_x
selftext:
I shared an early Fortigon release here previously. The project now has a free solo / four-player co-op demo and current builds for Windows, Linux, macOS and Android. I'm its creator, using Codex with Godot for coding, procedural model work, UI and effects.



The game lets you place and upgrade towers from above, then deploy a commander to fight alongside the defense in first person.



A concrete lesson from this iteration: making an animation look busier didn't make it better. An earlier pass made bodies wobble while feet took tiny, rapid steps. The follow-up used articulated joints and fixed-length limb movement, adjusted stride timing, and checked flying enemies and long-legged bosses separately. Detached feet and weapon pieces also needed actual in-engine inspection. AI-assisted implementation still needed repeated visual review and corrections.



We've also kept the demo's content restrictions and separate progression while updating it alongside the full game across all four platforms. The latest public release, v5.19.20, fixes wide Android screen fitting.



If you'd like to see the playable result, the free demo has one 15-wave map, all 10 towers and Vanguard / Artificer:

[https://xxragaxx.itch.io/fortigon?utm\_source=reddit&utm\_medium=community&utm\_campaign=demo\_outreach\_20261031&utm\_content=aigamedev\_update#demo](https://xxragaxx.itch.io/fortigon?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=community&utm_campaign=demo_outreach_20261031&utm_content=aigamedev_update#demo)



Gameplay footage: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CA\_o82iUYX4](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CA_o82iUYX4)



The full game is paid separately. Disclosure: this is self-promotion for my own game; AI assists coding and visual/content development and helped draft this post. For other AI-assisted game projects, how are you checking animation quality beyond whether it runs without errors?
